subject: Renewal negotiation: capacity firming + timebound credit request
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@numinalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.k@numinalabs.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: platform capacity + Q1 surge protection

Hi Marissa,

Hope you had a good holiday week. Our renewal for the platform is coming up end of January and the execs want to firm capacity and lock in protections for a Q1 product launch that will spike inference usage for six weeks.

We'd like to propose the following and get your guidance:
- Move from month-to-month to a 12-month committed plan pegged to ~700k token-equivalents/month (up from our current average of ~300k).
- Request a 60-day price hold for existing rates while we finalize PO and SOW.
- Ask for a one-time surge credit (applied post-invoice) to cover estimated 10% overage during the launch.

Can Redwood confirm high-level feasibility and any constraints? If this looks workable we'll share a draft SOW and updated usage estimates.

Thanks — appreciate a quick read.

Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Ops, Numina Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@numinalabs.com>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.k@numinalabs.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: platform capacity + Q1 surge protection

Tom — thanks for the clarity and happy to help. Short answer: we can structure a 12-month committed plan with temporary protections, but I need to loop in finance for the credit mechanics and sales ops for the timebound hold.

Quick thoughts:
- 700k/month committed looks fine from capacity planning — we can reserve GPU pools and set autoscaling thresholds.
- We can offer a 45–60 day price hold if PO is submitted within the hold window; exact length depends on billing cutoffs.
- Surge credit: we typically handle that as a one-time post-invoice credit tied to a documented launch window and an agreed overage cap.

I'll pull together a counter-proposal with concrete numbers and send an internal note. Can you share the launch window dates and an estimated peak QPS for the six-week period? That will help sizing.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: capacity + timebound credit ask — need pricing guidance

Ben / Lauren — forwarding the ask from Numina. Key asks: 12-month commit ~700k/mo, 45–60 day price hold while they finalize PO, and a one-time surge credit to cover ~10% overage during a six-week launch. Attached their basic renewal terms and SOW draft they mentioned.

Questions for pricing/ops:
1) For a 700k/month commit, what discount band do we recommend vs current list? They are current steady customer ~300k/mo.
2) Are we comfortable with a 60-day hold if they submit a PO within 30 days? Any billing cutoff concerns for month boundaries?
3) Surge credit approach: propose a capped credit equal to 30% of the forecasted overage cost (i.e., credit 30% of the extra tokens billed beyond committed usage during the six-week window) — would that be acceptable from finance?

I'm aiming to get a written counter by tomorrow EOD PST so we can keep the procurement timeline tight.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachments: Renewal_Term_Summary_v1.pdf, Numina_SOW_Draft.docx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 08:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: capacity + timebound credit ask — need pricing guidance

Marissa — good catch. My read:
- Discount: recommend a stepped discount tied to commit bands. For 700k/mo (annualized 8.4M token-equivalents) propose a 18% list discount year 1 with standard renewal escalator year 2 (unless they prepay). This is competitive and keeps margin.
- Price hold: 45 days is preferable since month-end billing cutoffs are tight; 60 days ok only if PO is routed through sales and procurement within 21 days. We should require the PO number and attach it to the DocuSign to trigger the hold.
- Surge credit: ok to approve a capped credit equal to 25% of overage cost (applied as post-invoice credit) — lower than your ask but protects margin. Require clear launch dates and a post-launch usage report signed by their ops lead.

If they want the 60-day without a hard PO, we need exec approval and a clause that credits are contingent on the PO arriving within 60 days.

Lauren — please confirm whether finance can accept 25% credit mechanics and provide the legal language for the PO-triggered price hold. If positive, Marissa I can draft the pricing sheet and updated SOW bullet.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Pricing
From: Priya Kapoor <priya.k@numinalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@numinalabs.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Jan 2027 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: platform capacity + Q1 surge protection

Marissa — thanks and appreciate the prompt response. We discussed internally and are OK with the proposed path provided the following are in the commercial terms:
- 12-month commit at 700k token-equivalents/month (reflecting our new product traffic forecast).
- 18% discount for year 1 off list and the 45-day formal price hold tied to PO submission (PO to be sent within 21 days).
- Surge support: accept the 25% capped post-invoice credit on documented overage for the six-week launch window (we'll provide a signed usage report).

Next steps: please send a counter with the updated pricing sheet, the PO-trigger clause language, and a DocuSign-ready SOW so procurement can route immediately. We attached a summary of launch dates and expected peak QPS in-line below.

Launch window: Feb 8 — Mar 21, 2027 (six weeks). Expected peak: 2.2k QPS sustained bursts during prime hour.

We'll look for the updated doc and aim to submit the PO within two weeks.

Best,
Priya Kapoor
Head of Product Operations, Numina Labs
